For the first time since the epidemic was declared in May, the numbers of people becoming infected is slowing down, according to officials.

Trump administration to seek extra funding from Congress to ‘dismantle’ Los Tiguerones over narcotics trafficking

Indonesian police are investigating the deaths of three Australians who died in Bali over the weekend, with initial reports suggesting a father killed his two young children before taking his own life.

Search and rescue agency says 107 people brought to safety from vessel hit by bad weather in Java Sea

Rescue workers in Indonesia said at least six people had died and 130 others were missing on Sunday after a ferry sailing between the islands of Java and Borneo capsized in bad weather.

One person has died and more than 30 are missing after a ferry sank off the coast of Vanuatu, the country’s government says.

The vessel, MV Matui, had set sail with more than 40 passengers and crew on Friday from the island of Santo to Ambae island in very rough seas, but did not arrive.

rfi.title: Workers across France stage protests over pay and rising costs
rfi.description: Protests are taking place across France on Tuesday, with fishermen, police officers, energy workers, university staff and other groups mobilising over a range of demands. Better pay, working conditions and the high cost of energy are among the main concerns.

rfi.title: Environmental activists angry over controversial AI data centre near Paris
rfi.description: France is preparing to build Europe’s largest artificial intelligence data centre in a village outside of Paris. The government hopes to boost its computing infrastructure and give France an edge in the global race to develop AI, but activists are concerned about the impacts on health and the environment.

rfi.title: NATO jets shoot down drone over Lithuania in latest Baltic security incident
rfi.description: NATO fighter jets shot have down a drone over Lithuania in the latest security incident on Europe's border with Russia as its war with Ukraine continues.

rfi.title: International justice 'can't be erased' despite US sanctions: ICC prosecutor
rfi.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) is facing US sanctions since deciding to issue arrest warrants over alleged war crimes in Gaza. Mame Mandiaye Niang, the Senegalese magistrate who has been acting head of the ICC's Office of the Prosecutor since his predecessor Karim Khan was forced out, tells RFI that while the Court's resilience is being tested, its existence is not under threat.

rfi.title: Finland joins French nuclear umbrella amid European security push
rfi.description: Finland has decided to join France’s nuclear deterrence umbrella in a bid to bolster regional security in the face of uncertainty over the United States' commitment to Europe and NATO.

rfi.title: France says Russia seeks to 'intimidate' EU with train attack near Poland
rfi.description: France and the European Union have condemned a Russian strike on a passenger train on the Polish border that has raised concerns about the risks of the war spreading closer to EU and NATO territory.

rfi.title: France seeks EU backing for revised social media ban for under-15s
rfi.description: A month after France’s Constitutional Council struck down a proposed social media ban for under-15s, the government has submitted a new version that President Emmanuel Macron wants passed before he leaves office in the spring.

rfi.title: World in Frames: RFI traces the stories behind the world's most famous photos
rfi.description: As France marks 200 years since inventor Nicéphore Niépce took the world’s oldest surviving photograph, RFI looks back at photos that changed our view of history – or even history itself. Here we tell the story of how a portrait of an unnamed woman came to represent the suffering of a nation in Dorothea Lange’s Migrant Mother, and what the iconic picture left out.

rfi.title: 'Historic day' for Nigeria as Dangote oil refinery launches IPO
rfi.description: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote on Monday launched what is slated as Africa's biggest initial public offering (IPO), which aims to raise $1.6 billion (€1.3 billion) to expand his mega oil refinery to become the world's largest.

rfi.title: Growing budgets show Africa keen to defend its place in the space race
rfi.description: African states invest around $500 million in space programmes annually, a figure expected to reach around $40 billion by 2030. With a number of initiatives already in place, the continent is seeking a seat at the table when it comes to international decisions on space exploration and equal access to the development of technology.

rfi.title: Normandy derailment inquiry widens focus on rail fragment found on track
rfi.description: A technical investigation has been launched into the derailment of a regional train near Rouen that left 44 people injured, as authorities work to establish how a piece of rail came to be lying on the track.

rfi.title: Sweden's election too close to call, left opposition narrowly leads
rfi.description: Sweden's general election is still too close to call, with Magdalena Andersson’s centre-left opposition coalition holding a narrow lead over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson’s right-wing alliance.

rfi.title: Macron, Carney to visit French Atlantic islands with sovereignty message to Trump
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney will visit the French North Atlantic territory of Saint-Pierre-and-Miquelon next week, in a symbolic show of support for national sovereignty amid renewed territorial claims by US President Donald Trump.

rfi.title: France moves to defuse US row over UN social media post
rfi.description: France has expressed regret over a social media post questioning the United States’ commitment to human rights, in a move expected to clear the way for its new ambassador to take up his post in Washington.

rfi.title: French Rafale jets take flight for 40,000-kilometre mission over three-continents
rfi.description: Four French Rafale fighter jets have embarked on a 40-day mission spanning three continents, highlighting France’s ability to deploy its air power around the world while strengthening cooperation with key international partners.

rfi.title: Radio France staff strike over appointment of right-wing magazine editor
rfi.description: Radio France staff began a two-day strike on Sunday over France Inter’s decision to hire a senior editor from the right-wing magazine Valeurs actuelles as a political commentator. Charles Sapin’s appointment has drawn criticism because the magazine has previously been convicted of racist public insult and incitement to racial hatred.

rfi.title: As catches dwindle, Congo River fishermen turn to plastic waste
rfi.description: On the Congo River, plastic is becoming the catch of the day. Some fishermen around Kinshasa, capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo, can now make more money pulling plastic from the water than catching fish, as declining catches and growing waste pollution threaten an artisanal way of life.

rfi.title: From townships to TikTok, South Africa's amapiano gets the world dancing
rfi.description: Amapiano dancers across South Africa are helping a sound born in the country's black townships reach audiences far beyond its borders – one viral challenge at a time. Short routines filmed in homes, schools and public spaces are spreading across social media, giving musicians another way to promote a genre that's now a global hit.

euronews.title: How Belarus helps Russia and its drone arsenal target Ukraine and threaten NATO
euronews.description: Belarus appears to have resumed providing infrastructure to support Russian drone attacks on Ukraine and is now also emerging as a threat to NATO after a drone flying from Belarus was shot down over Lithuania. Here's what we know.

euronews.title: Suspected sabotage brings Dutch rail network to a standstill on Budget Day
euronews.description: A wave of coordinated rail sabotage paralysed Dutch trains on Budget Day as the government calls for an investigation to reveal the perpetrators.

euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this September 15th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: Twenty-five years on, Dubai's media bet has become a global platform
euronews.description: This year’s Arab Media Summit in Dubai, now in its 25th year, is more than just an event organised by the city, says Mona Ghane l Marri in an OpEd for Euronews. It has evolved into a shared platform for an industry that has become more diverse, more global and more interconnected.

euronews.title: EU has 'the power' to lead on 'global treaty on AI', says MEP Brando Benifei
euronews.description: MEP Brando Benifei says citizens "need to be worried" about AI, warning of "real risks" such as the "loss of control".

euronews.title: Danish PM condemns Russian flare attack on helicopter as 'reckless'
euronews.description: A routine patrol over the Baltic turned dangerous, adding to a run of close encounters between Russian forces and NATO members this year.

euronews.title: UN urges full access for investigators as Gaza death toll mounts
euronews.description: A UN access request over Gaza's uncounted dead raises questions that could shape how this war is judged.

euronews.title: Iran's new ayatollah is a Nolan fan interested in start-ups, in-laws say
euronews.description: Six months after succeeding his father, Mojtaba Khamenei has made no public appearances, yet his late wife's family has described him to state-affiliated outlets as a film buff familiar with Christopher Nolan, interested in start-ups and cognitive science, and diligent about learning English.

euronews.title: China's retail sales slow again as Beijing struggles to revive consumer spending
euronews.description: Retail sales in China grew just 0.4% in August, the slowest pace since growth resumed and the second consecutive monthly slowdown, underlining how little progress Beijing has made in reviving consumer spending even as factory output accelerates.

euronews.title: Thirty years on, what is left of the French Touch?
euronews.description: French Touch has never been so widely acclaimed. Now hailed as a "national pride", the movement still divides over what it is today and what it leaves to future generations.

euronews.title: EU institutions face budget cuts as member states scramble for money
euronews.description: The money allocated for the EU institutions is emerging as a target for cuts in ongoing budgetary discussions, according to a confidential document seen by Euronews.

euronews.title: Microsoft introduces AI guardrails for US schools amid growing backlash
euronews.description: OpenAI and Anthropic said they also were discussing safety and privacy pacts with the American teachers’ union. But Google, the dominant provider of education technology for US schools, has not said whether it plans to offer similar protections.

euronews.title: Enter the hoax buster: Trump dismisses AI concerns as Europe and China fret
euronews.description: US President Donald Trump has dismissed AI extinction fears as a "hoax," casting himself as the only safeguard the world needs, as Europe and China both call for guardrails on the fast-moving technology.

euronews.title: Benjamin Netanyahu joins Israeli ministers attacking Venice-winning documentary 'NAZA'
euronews.description: The documentary 'NAZA', which won the Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival, examines Israel's targeting practices in Gaza and alleges that mass civilian deaths are routinely factored into decisions over military strikes.

euronews.title: No, the EU isn't demanding that Ukraine mobilise women against Russia's invasion
euronews.description: Ukraine's counter-disinformation agency says that the claims originated with Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service.

euronews.title: Emmy record for Matthew Rhys as Welshman's Widow's Bay collected three awards
euronews.description: Widow's Bay actor Matthew Rhys celebrated setting a new record at the Emmy Awards with a speech in Welsh as he thanked his home country for producing extraordinary talents.

euronews.title: Most Europeans say a second language is useful. Not everyone can actually speak one
euronews.description: A YouGov survey of six European countries reveals wide gaps in language fluency, motivation to learn, and views on compulsory language education.

euronews.title: FLEX satellite in orbit: studying plant responses to climate change from space
euronews.description: The mission will study photosynthesis and how vegetation responds to climate change, while the new Sentinel-3C monitors oceans, land, ice and the atmosphere.

lemonde.title: Ciblée par les drones ukrainiens, l’économie russe montre de plus en plus de signes de faiblesse
lemonde.description: Les attaques de Kiev sur les raffineries et les entrepôts commerciaux ont fait entrer la guerre dans le quotidien des Russes, à la veille des élections législatives qui doivent se tenir du 18 au 20 septembre. Si l’économie reste relativement résiliente, les problèmes se multiplient, inflation en tête.

lemonde.title: Anne Hidalgo fait part de ses « regrets immenses » à propos des violences dans le périscolaire à Paris
lemonde.description: L’ancienne maire de Paris est auditionnée au Sénat, mardi, qui enquête sur les violences sexuelles dans le périscolaire en France. « Nos institutions ont failli », a-t-elle également affirmé.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Edouard Philippe, Gabriel Attal et Bruno Retailleau pris au piège de la dispersion
lemonde.description: Les trois prétendants à l’Elysée sont engagés dans une guerre de position à droite et au centre. La fragmentation inquiète les cadres et les élus de leurs formations politiques, alors que plane la menace d’un second tour entre Marine Le Pen et Jean-Luc Mélenchon.

lemonde.title: Au procès de l’assassinat de l’ancien rugbyman Federico Martin Aramburu, une terrible journée pour les accusés
lemonde.description: Avec les dépositions de la mère et des plus proches amis de la victime, lundi, à la cour d’assises de Paris, un contraste saisissant s’est imposé entre l’international argentin et le parcours de violence de Loïk Le Priol et de Romain Bouvier.

lemonde.title: Prix des carburants : le dépôt pétrolier de Fos-sur-Mer de nouveau accessible, après un blocage des pêcheurs
lemonde.description: Les comités régionaux des pêches du sud de la France, les organisations de producteurs de Méditerranée et des syndicats de la profession ont lancé lundi un mouvement commun pour protester contre la hausse des coûts d’exploitation.

lemonde.title: Après la réforme des concours, le désarroi des centaines d’enseignants contractuels privés de poste à la rentrée 2026
lemonde.description: La session de recrutement 2026, qui voyait cohabiter deux concours dans le cadre de la réforme de la formation, a conduit à un afflux de stagiaires dans les établissements. Pour la première fois, des contractuels, parfois en poste depuis des années, n’ont pas été renouvelés faute de places.

lemonde.title: Le mariage du fils aîné de Donald Trump aux Bahamas sponsorisé par un homme d’affaires russe
lemonde.description: Le généreux contributeur, Umar Kremlev, un proche des cercles du pouvoir à Moscou, dirige la fédération controversée International Boxing Association et est aussi présent dans le secteur lucratif des paris sportifs en ligne.

lemonde.title: TotalEnergies s’allie à Mistral pour révolutionner l’exploration pétrolière grâce à l’intelligence artificielle
lemonde.description: Avec un partenariat de 100 millions d’euros sur trois ans, TotalEnergies et Mistral veulent notamment optimiser la gestion des réservoirs de pétrole et de gaz.

lemonde.title: Le projet d’extension des aéroports parisiens se poursuit, malgré les oppositions
lemonde.description: Alors que plusieurs associations environnementales espèrent bloquer le développement des aéroports d’Orly et, surtout, de Roissy-Charles-de-Gaulle, les compagnies aériennes se sont, à une courte majorité, prononcées en faveur de ce programme à 8,2 milliards d’euros.

lemonde.title: « Chouette d’or » : l’organisateur du jeu Michel Becker perd son procès en diffamation contre un joueur
lemonde.description: Michel Becker attaquait en justice le président d’une association de joueurs, pour des propos publiés en ligne critiquant l’organisation de la célèbre chasse au trésor.

lemonde.title: Comment mettre fin au « plafond de mère », cette pénalité dans la carrière des femmes ?
lemonde.description: Un rapport du Haut conseil à l’égalité entre les femmes et les hommes relève que la naissance d’un enfant entraîne pour les mères une chute de revenu salarial de 40 % et propose 45 mesures pour lutter contre les discriminations, explique Jules Thomas, journaliste au service Economie du « Monde ».

lemonde.title: Le rappeur Macklemore annonce avoir été écarté de la tournée d’Ed Sheeran après des propos propalestiniens
lemonde.description: Sous la pression de plusieurs salles américaines, Macklemore a été retiré de la tournée d’Ed Sheeran, illustrant la difficulté pour les artistes de s’exprimer sur le conflit israélo-palestinien.

lemonde.title: Quand une banque chinoise soutient le nickel russe pendant la guerre en Ukraine
lemonde.description: Des documents confidentiels révèlent comment l’Industrial and Commercial Bank of China a courtisé des entreprises à haut risque, tel un géant russe du nickel, secteur frappé en 2024 par les sanctions occidentales, pour garantir des ressources et des alliances au régime de Xi Jinping.

lemonde.title: Tourisme : derrière le record des recettes, le décrochage des Français
lemonde.description: La fréquentation et les recettes internationales ont progressé cet été. Mais la clientèle française est moins partie en juillet et août, a raccourci ses séjours et réduit ses dépenses, en raison des tensions sur le pouvoir d’achat et des canicules

lemonde.title: Emoi à Anticor, sous la menace d’une mise sous tutelle par la justice
lemonde.description: Le tribunal judiciaire de Versailles a désigné, vendredi 11 septembre, un administrateur provisoire pour gérer l’association anticorruption. Mais cette décision, qui n’a pas été assortie d’une exécution provisoire, n’est pas immédiatement applicable. Anticor annonce faire appel.

lemonde.title: Le Pentagone reconnaît pour la première fois une pénurie de munitions pour l’armée américaine, du fait de la guerre en Iran
lemonde.description: Alors que Donald Trump assurait encore début septembre que les Etats-Unis disposaient de « quantités pratiquement illimitées de munitions », un rapport du ministère de la défense américain relève « une pénurie sur les inventaires stratégiques » après le lancement de l’opération « Fureur épique » en Iran.

france24fr.title: Canada–États-Unis : l’escalade commerciale pousse Ottawa à changer de cap
france24fr.description: Une nouvelle série de droits de douane américains frappe des produits canadiens. Face à une guerre commerciale qui s’intensifie, Ottawa cherche à réduire sa dépendance aux États-Unis en se rapprochant notamment de l’Europe et de l’Asie.

france24fr.title: Mbappé, Yamal, Dembélé, Kane ? La campagne pour le Ballon d'or bat son plein
france24fr.description: À deux semaines de la clôture des votes pour le Ballon d’Or, les principaux candidats au titre de meilleur joueur de l'année font campagne.

france24fr.title: L'Ukraine prendra des "mesures de désescalade" si la Russie fait de même, affirme Zelensky
france24fr.description: Le président Volodymyr Zelensky a affirmé lundi que l'Ukraine était prête à prendre des "mesures de désescalade" si la Russie en faisait de même, sans confirmer l'affirmation de Donald Trump selon laquelle Moscou et Kiev ont accepté de ne plus frapper d'infrastructures énergétiques.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie occupée : une ONG accuse Israël de vouloir "éliminer" les Palestiniens
france24fr.description: Une ONG israélienne a accusé lundi les autorités israéliennes de mener une politique visant à "éliminer" les Palestiniens en tant que peuple, en multipliant notamment les violences et les restrictions en Cisjordanie occupée.

france24fr.title: Prix du carburant : des pêcheurs mécontents bloquent un dépôt pétrolier à Fos-sur-Mer
france24fr.description: Un dépôt pétrolier à Fos-sur-Mer est bloqué depuis mardi matin par des dizaines de pêcheurs. La profession proteste contre "la hausse des coûts d'exploitation et du carburant", liée au conflit au Moyen-Orient.

france24fr.title: Donald Trump Junior, mariage à la russe
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce mardi 15 septembre, l’envolée des cours du pétrole, provoquée par la paralysie du détroit d’Ormuz et l’offensive des Houthis en mer rouge. Le mariage de Donald Trump Junior financé par un «homme d’affaires» russe proche du Kremlin. La mobilisation, en France, pour demander plus de moyens face au changement climatique. La controverse, en Israël, autour du documentaire «Naza». Un (nouveau) scandale autour de l’actrice Sydney Sweeney. Et les bienfaits de la lecture.

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis en manque de munitions à cause de la guerre en Iran
france24fr.description: Après sept mois de conflit contre l'Iran, le Pentagone a reconnu lundi pour la première fois "une pénurie de munitions". Dans un rapport, le ministère américain de la Défense évoque quelque 22,3 milliards dépensés uniquement en munitions tirées, pour un coût global de 33,4 milliards.

france24fr.title: Olivier Grondeau, de l'enfer des prisons iraniennes à la première sélection du Goncourt
france24fr.description: Arrêté en Iran en 2022 et détenu pendant deux ans et demi, Olivier Grondeau raconte son expérience carcérale dans "Joseph dans la nuit" (L’Iconoclaste). Un récit nourri de ses rencontres en prison, qui figure dans la première sélection du prix Goncourt 2026.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : le Pentagone reconnait une "pénurie" de munitions avec la guerre en Iran
Pourquoi les forces yéménites n’ont-elles pas réussi à stopper l’offensive des Houthis ?
france24fr.description: Les forces gouvernementales yéménites, pourtant soutenues militairement et financièrement par l’Arabie saoudite, ont cédé en quelques jours face à l’offensive des Houthis sur la côte de la mer Rouge. Une victoire qui est autant le produit de leur propre discipline que de la désunion persistante du camp gouvernemental.

france24fr.title: En direct : un drone abattu en Lituanie par l’Otan, un hélicoptère danois visé par des fusées éclairantes russes
france24fr.description: Un drone survolant la Lituanie a été détruit dans la nuit de lundi à mardi par des chasseurs de l'Otan, a annoncé le président lituanien. Selon la radio nationale lituanienne, le drone était venu de la Biélorussie voisine et se dirigeait vers l'Ouest. Un hélicoptère danois survolant la mer Baltique a été visé lundi soir par des fusées éclairantes lancées par une frégate russe. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: En direct : "Aucune discussion" avec les États-Unis, l’Iran répond sèchement à Trump
france24fr.description: Téhéran a rejeté mardi tout dialogue en l'état avec Washington, après que Donald Trump s'est dit "ouvert" à la discussion. Sur le plan opérationnel, le Pentagone a reconnu une "pénurie" de munitions liée à la guerre, un constat que la Maison Blanche avait pourtant refusé de confirmer ces derniers mois. Par ailleurs, l'Arabie saoudite a promis de riposter après de nouvelles attaques des Houthis du Yémen contre son territoire. Notre direct.

france24fr.title: La Cour suprême contrecarre les plans de Donald Trump sur le vote par correspondance
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a essuyé lundi un nouvel échec dans la bataille judiciaire autour du vote par correspondance aux États-Unis, à quelques semaines des élections de mi-mandat. La Cour suprême à majorité conservatrice a rejeté un recours de l'administration concernant un décret visant à encadrer davantage le vote postal.

france24fr.title: Les séries "Widow's Bay" et "The Pitt" triomphent aux Emmy Awards
france24fr.description: La comédie d'épouvante "Widow's Bay" a dominé la cérémonie des Emmy Awards lundi soir à Los Angeles, tandis que "The Pitt" a remporté pour la deuxième année consécutive le titre de meilleure série dramatique. La soirée a aussi vu Jean Smart décrocher un cinquième Emmy pour son rôle dans "Hacks".

france24fr.title: Invité par Washington, le Venezuela va participer au G20 consacré à l'énergie
france24fr.description: Caracas participe cette semaine à la réunion des ministres de l'Énergie du G20 à Houston, sur l'invitation des États-Unis, alors que Donald Trump cherche à revigorer l'exploitation des immenses réserves pétrolières du Venezuela.

france24fr.title: Houthis : les nouveaux maîtres de la mer Rouge ?
france24fr.description: En l’espace de quelques jours, à l’issue d’une offensive éclair, les insurgés houthis, pro-iraniens, ont pris le contrôle de l’ensemble du littoral yéménite de la mer Rouge. Déjà vendredi, il s'étaient emparés du stratégique détroit de Bab el-Mandeb. Autrefois simple guérilla de montagne, les insurgés d’Ansar Allah s'imposent de plus en plus sur la scène internationale.

france24fr.title: Espace : les États-Unis confirment pour la première fois avoir déployé des armes en orbite
france24fr.description: L'US Space Force a annoncé lundi posséder des "systèmes de contrôle spatial armés" capables de défendre les forces américaines contre des actions hostiles. Washington justifie ce déploiement par la montée en puissance de la Chine et de la Russie dans ce domaine.

france24fr.title: L'Ukraine se dit prête à des "mesures de désescalade" si la Russie en fait de même
france24fr.description: Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky a évoqué lundi une possible désescalade dans la guerre contre l'invasion russe, sans confirmer l'affirmation de Donald Trump selon laquelle Kiev et Moscou auraient accepté un arrêt mutuel des frappes sur les infrastructures énergétiques.

zeit.description: Wenn München 2031 die Leichtathletik-WM ausrichtet, rechnet die Stadt mit Kosten in Höhe von rund 110 Millionen Euro. Es ist die dritte Leichtathletik-WM in Deutschland.

zeit.description: Seit dem Trauma von 2012 hofft der FC Bayern darauf, in der heimischen Allianz Arena die Champions League zu gewinnen. 2028 haben die Bayern wieder die Chance.

observador.description: Quatro mil pessoas continuam desaparecidas no país, incluindo 610 estrangeiros, quase três semanas depois da enxurrada. Entre os desaparecidos, há duas portuguesas.

observador.description: Taxa de inflação homóloga é a mais elevada desde 2023. A subida dos preços em agosto deveu-se sobretudo ao aumento do preço dos combustíveis. Espanha anuncia desconto de 20 cêntimos nos combustíveis.

observador.description: As medidas incluem dar prioridade de estacionamento aos residentes e fazer com que as pessoas percebam que "tem de ser mais compensador andar de transporte público do que de transporte individual".

observador.description: Filinto Lima elogia a estratégia que resolveu a falta de vagas nas escolas de Lisboa. O Presidente da Associação de Escolas Públicas pede no entanto, um reforço do número de turmas no futuro.

spiegel.title: Stuttgart 21: Gutachter zweifelt an eigener Studie zu Großprojekt der Deutschen Bahn

spiegel.title: Jürgen Klopp beim DFB: Diese sechs neuen Spieler könnten Klopps Probleme lösen

spiegel.title: Leichtathletik: München wird Gastgeber der WM 2031

spiegel.title: Bundeslagebild 2025: Gewalt als Dienstleistung, ausgeführt von Minderjährigen

spiegel.title: Bundesgerichtshof: Die Maskenprozesse sind für die Bundesregierung eine Zeitbombe

spiegel.title: Harald Schmidt rät Friedrich Merz zu offensiverem Auftreten

phys-org.description: Emotional mechanisms are frequently used to inspire good environmental behavior. But how effective are they at inspiring actual sustainable change? And in his view, conflict is coming to space, making it all more urgent.

undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA

Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

proj-syn.title: The People Not Worth Replacing
proj-syn.description: At first glance, MAGA’s fear of immigrants and the rest of America’s fear of data centers have many similarities, with each reflecting insecurities about one’s place in a changing economy. But while the first fear tells natives that their place is valuable, the second assumes that it will soon be worth nothing.

proj-syn.title: What Amodei’s Call for an AI Pause Gets Wrong
proj-syn.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s recent appeal for a pause on AI development is a welcome one. But while AI companies do indeed need more breathing space to consider the full impact of their inventions before releasing them to the market, self-interested oversight is not the kind of governance we need.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Asset Europe Has Overlooked
proj-syn.description: Europe’s soil is gradually dying, and yet the continent has still not recognized it as a strategic asset. Fortunately, the EU has many of the tools it needs to act, but doing so will require an overarching framework that helps farmers access financial rewards for measurable soil outcomes.

proj-syn.title: Who Is Responsible for Nepal’s Tragedy?
proj-syn.description: The devastating floods in Nepal demonstrate what happens when reckless development puts climate-vulnerable communities in harm’s way. They also highlight a climate-finance system that is unable to provide the funds countries need in the immediate aftermath of such disasters.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Choose Between Power and Dependence
proj-syn.description: European citizens do not want “more Europe” in the abstract, but rather a European Union that is capable of protecting, investing, anticipating, deciding, and acting whenever national-level policymaking is insufficient. In today’s world, ensuring citizens’ control over their future requires the freedom to act together.

proj-syn.title: Progressive Economics Is Delivering
proj-syn.description: By combining fiscal responsibility, growth, and social development, progressive governments in Brazil and Spain have improved millions of people’s lives and refuted the hoary belief that conservatives are better stewards of the economy. Such a successful alternative model could not have come at a better time.

proj-syn.title: The Agentic Information Economy
proj-syn.description: An internet populated and run by AI agents will need not just reliable data but also a broader information ecology capable of questioning its own inputs and transmitting corrections where they are needed if information changes. But whether this will serve private interests or the public good remains to be seen.

proj-syn.title: Who Owns What AI Learns?
proj-syn.description: Since frontier AI models have already consumed much of the readily available stock of public knowledge on the internet, what remains is the valuable tacit knowledge embedded within organizations. Whoever sets the terms of how this knowledge is teased out and transferred will set the terms of the next economy.

proj-syn.title: America First Is Jeopardizing Taiwan’s Greatest Asset
proj-syn.description: Rather than strengthening Taiwan, US demands for market access, technology investment, and defense capabilities are deepening political polarization and eroding the island’s ability to build consensus just when it needs it most. The timing could hardly be worse.

proj-syn.title: Technology Is Not Above the Law
proj-syn.description: In arguing for a regulatory regime that is skewed entirely toward freeing developers to build online services, rather than placing any social obligations on them, the AI industry is using a playbook that Silicon Valley wrote 30 years ago. This time, however, the public seems less inclined to buy the industry's argument.

proj-syn.title: China’s Platform State and the AI Race
proj-syn.description: Balancing regulation with innovation is never easy, and the Chinese government’s robust support for AI could lead to inefficiency and excess. But the “platform state” model, combined with other strengths, has enabled China to achieve dominance in multiple strategic sectors, while enhancing its resilience.

proj-syn.title: Which Future for Online Life?
proj-syn.description: By articulating a vision of the future that seems inevitable, technology industry leaders want to create the impression that the surrender of privacy and other defining trends of the current moment cannot be stopped. But predictions become self-fulfilling prophecies only if we believe them and act accordingly.

proj-syn.title: When Words Are No Longer for Us
proj-syn.description: Owing to the proliferation of large language models throughout our software and social systems, we are now undergoing a textpocalypse, marked by not just a deluge of slop but a fundamental unmooring of language and text from lived human experience. The first victim is likely to be the internet itself.

proj-syn.title: Who Will Do the World’s “Most Impossible Job”?
proj-syn.description: Although the United Nations is facing a financial and political crisis that is almost certain to get worse before it gets better, the field of candidates vying for the organization’s top job is surprisingly crowded. If history is any guide, power politics, more than anything else, will decide the outcome.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Pro-Human Vision
proj-syn.description: The original vision of the internet as a democratizing force failed to account for the manner in which power would concentrate, attention would be monetized, and public discourse would be manipulated. In Europe and elsewhere, these lessons now must inform how we govern generative AI.

proj-syn.title: Superintelligent Democracy
proj-syn.description: Rather than framing the pursuit of AI capabilities as a race, we should turn the process into a democratic mission, with milestones set by the people, rather than on their behalf. Taiwan's own demonstration of mission-led governance, along with insights from the open-web community, show what is possible.

proj-syn.title: Will We Preserve the Sources of Human Learning?
proj-syn.description: By obscuring or destroying the primary sources of knowledge, large language models create the illusion of an embodied and active collection of everything we know. But without examining and interrogating the human originators of recorded knowledge and wisdom, one cannot fully develop one’s own understanding.

proj-syn.title: AI Is Fracking the Open Web
proj-syn.description: The demand for what digital publishers offer is real and robust, but the old methods of managing it will no longer work when cyberspace is inundated with bots designed to extract value wherever it can be found. Building an alternative will fall to the remaining advocates of the old open web.
